title: slim connector: credential fanout and async-generator UX
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a compact credential delegator and refactors async-generator streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible; minor version bumps for all SDKs. See migration notes in PR body.
description:
Context and motivation: We have several SDK ergonomics gaps that customers hit when they try to wire credentials together with streaming connectors and retry policies. This PR introduces a slim CredentialDelegator (language-agnostic contract with tiny implementations in py/ts/go) and consolidates generator/pullstream ergonomics so users get consistent cancel/resume/reauth behavior across SDKs.

Summary of changes:
1) Introduce CredentialDelegator abstraction and lightweight token fanout strategy to reduce hot-path allocations on high-throughput streaming.
2) Rework async-generator/pullstream helpers: add pause(), resume(), and graceful_close() helpers on generator wrappers and unify the backoff hooks used by the SDKs.
3) Tighten retry semantics for streaming reconnects (hedged retry floor + jitter) and expose a small set of retry presets.
4) Minor API surface alignment across Python, TypeScript, and Go; bump package versions (py 0.13.0 -> 0.14.0, ts 1.27.0 -> 1.28.0, go v1.5.2 -> v1.6.0).
5) Add telemetry hooks for credential exchange so we can measure stalled reauth events.

Checklist:
- [x] API proposal (linked Linear ENG-1893)
- [x] Implementation in Python SDK (py/sdk/connector.py, py/sdk/auth/delegator.py)
- [x] Implementation in TypeScript SDK (ts/src/connector.ts, ts/src/cred/delegator.ts)
- [x] Implementation in Go SDK (go/connector/connector.go, go/cred/delegator.go)
- [x] Unit tests added for reconnect/backoff and credential fallback
- [x] Integration test in benchmark-lab to validate latency impact
- [x] Docs snippet and migration notes added to README and changelogs

Design notes:
- CredentialDelegator provides two methods: GetToken(ctx) and Subscribe(ctx, channel) where Subscribe returns a small typed channel/iterator for token updates; implementations are intentionally minimal so embedding layers can add caching or pinning.
- Streaming helpers normalize close semantics: consumers can call graceful_close() to attempt flush then cancel; pause()/resume() allow user-controlled backpressure without tearing the session (useful for UI-driven consumers).
- Retry presets are defaults (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and can be overridden per-client or per-connector.

Backwards compatibility: Existing SDK surface remains supported; the delegator is additive and the default credential provider is a thin shim that wraps existing token providers.

Migration notes:
- Python: replace custom reconnect loops with the new generator_wrapper() helper (examples/py/migrate_streams.md).
- TypeScript: add a small adapter that calls credDelegator.subscribe() for long-lived pages; existing sync token flows still work.
- Go: use the NewCredDelegatorFromProvider(provider) helper to avoid refactor at call sites.

Commits (high level):
- "introduce credential delegator interfaces and tests"
- "add generator wrapper helpers with pause/resume/close"
- "ts: implement delegator and adapter; add tests"
- "go: implement delegator and connector; fix race in stream cancel"
- "docs: migration notes and changelogs"

Files changed (high level):
- py/sdk/auth/delegator.py (new)
- py/sdk/connector.py (refactor generator helpers)
- py/tests/test_stream_reconnect.py (new tests)
- ts/src/cred/delegator.ts (new)
- ts/src/connector.ts (refactor)
- ts/test/stream_reconnect.test.ts (new)
- go/cred/delegator.go (new)
- go/connector/connector.go (refactor)
- go/connector/connector_test.go (new)
- docs/quickstarts/streaming-migration.md (docs)
- examples/py/migrate_streams.md (examples)
- examples/ts/migrate_streams.md (examples)
- benchmark-lab/recipes/streaming_cred_perf.yml (perf test)

Testing & CI:
- Local unit tests: py 124 passed, ts 78 passed, go 64 passed.
- Benchmark-lab results: end-to-end 99th latency regression <1.8% on a simulated 1k rps stream workload; median latency unchanged.
- CI: linux unit matrix and integration job passed, flake8/linting fixes applied in a follow-up commit.

Review conversation (high level):
- Samir: "Can you ensure delegator Subscribe() is GC-safe and doesn't leak goroutines?" -> Author: "Added a finalizer-based test in go/connector/connector_test.go and adjusted tearDown to close channels deterministically."
- Lena: "I see a small race on stream cancel in the go tests; did you run with -race?" -> Author: "Yes, fixed with a small mutex around the shutdown path; added race-flag CI job for Go."
- Ethan: "Docs look good; please include a short migration snippet for the TS SDK showing the adapter." -> Author: "Added examples/ts/migrate_streams.md demonstrating the adapter."

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- We preserved the existing auth shim for legacy consumers; follow-up work will add an LRU prefix token cache for low-latency hot-paths (ENG-2018).
- Edge case: very-high-churn credential providers can hit a token notification storm; we added basic de-dup in delegator but the follow-up will add batching at the connector.

Observability:
- Emit telemetry event cred.delegate.swap and cred.delegate.stall when a reauth is delayed > 500ms.
- Added a debug metric stream.reconnect.attempts per-client for canarying.

Impact and rationale:
- This change reduces per-stream allocation by ~12% in microbenchmarks and provides a consistent developer experience across SDKs for streaming flows with reauth/reconnect.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Samir and Lena and CI green. Backported to release/1.28 for TypeScript and release/0.14 for Python in separate PRs.

Migration action items for customers:
- If you rely on custom reconnect loops, switch to generator_wrapper to benefit from consistent backoff and graceful shutdown.
- If you manage tokens externally and observe rare stalls, enable telemetry and file an issue referencing ENG-2018.
